A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same adaptive visual-program reasoning research, substantially revised and renamed from FS-VisPR to VideoPro. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations, and appendices are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original VideoQA benchmark results, confidence analyses, module and parameter-search ablations, and successful and failed reasoning examples.

after.justification: v3 reports original results on four benchmarks, accuracy and runtime comparisons, training and refinement ablations, and execution-mode analyses.

M1.justification: v1 uses a separate FS-LLM program controller, module-parameter search, and fallback to fast answering after execution failure. v3 trains a unified VideoLLM for native/program routing and introduces program correction using execution logs or low-confidence predictions. Its new reason-and-refine supervision and SFT-plus-GRPO training substantially change both learning and inference (Sections 3.4-3.6).

E1.justification: v3 adds evaluation on MLVU, described as a multi-task long-video benchmark, while retaining CG-Bench training and the three original evaluation benchmarks. This extends coverage within the existing long-video domain; short-, medium-, and long-duration analyses remain represented.

E2.justification: The main comparison expands to OpenAI o3, native Qwen3-VL-8B, two distinct VideoAgent methods, and VideoTree. The agentic methods participate in the retained VideoMME comparison, not merely the added MLVU benchmark. LongVILA plus Video-RAG and Qwen2.5VL-7B-RAG disappear from the comparison (v1 Table 3; v3 Table 1).

E3.justification: The reported training regimen changes from three SFT epochs on 5K examples to one SFT epoch on 5K trajectories followed by one GRPO epoch on 10K samples. Data synthesis changes from GPT-4.1 to GPT-5, and evaluated model configurations change. The native Qwen2.5-VL-7B comparator uses 128 frames in v1 and 64 in v3. New paradigm comparisons measure runtime alongside accuracy and output length.

E4.justification: v3 adds native-versus-program-versus-adaptive reasoning comparisons with runtime, refinement controls, SFT-versus-GRPO ablations, and grouped module-removal tests (Tables 2-4). These replace v1's parameter-search aggregation and detailed parameter-sensitivity experiments. Confidence-threshold, duration, and routing analyses are revised, while v1's illustrated failure cases are removed and new refinement cases appear.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run or seed counts, error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests for benchmark estimates. Per-answer confidence guides inference in both versions; it is not uncertainty reporting for experimental performance.

E6.justification: For the system using Qwen2.5-VL-7B, v1 Table 3 reports 50.4/62.2/62.2 on LVBench/VideoMME-long/LongVideoBench; v3 Table 1 reports 47.2/56.7/60.9 under revised method and training conditions, so these are not matched-setting performance losses. v3 adds Qwen3-VL-8B and MLVU results plus extensive timing and ablation results. Existing baseline entries also change, including Gemini-1.5-pro's VideoMME value from 77.4 to 67.4.

T1.justification: v3 adds mathematical definitions of the weighted GRPO reward (Equation 3) and binary mode-consistency reward (Appendix A.3). The decoded-token confidence formula and correct/high-confidence routing-label principle are retained. Neither version develops theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The main contributions shift from aligning an open-source program controller and improving programs through parameter search to jointly learning adaptive routing and execution/confidence-guided self-refinement in a unified VideoLLM. GRPO-based learning and learned error recovery become central claims. The headline empirical claim shifts to average improvements over native VideoLLM backbones, including 6.7 points for Qwen3-VL-8B.

C2.justification: v3 introduces substantive interpretations involving learned error correction, GRPO reward alignment, global-context contributions, and smaller gains on benchmarks containing easier short-video questions. It adds limitations concerning manual module integration and transfer to new domains, plus hallucination and teacher-bias risks. The overconfidence limitation already present in v1 Appendix A.4 is retained, not newly discovered.

D1.justification: v3 substantially revises reproducibility documentation through separate routing and repair prompts, an API listing, reward specifications, and an explicit generation temperature (Appendices A.1-A.3). The documented software changes from LLaMAFactory/vLLM to MS-SWIFT, while v1's disclosure of up to four H100 GPUs disappears. Ten-second clipping, LanguageBind, DEVA, and EasyOCR were already documented in v1 and are retained details.

R1.justification: Related work shifts from broad LLM code generation, planning, and dual-process motivation toward learned adaptation and feedback-based refinement. New references include Self-Refine, De-fine, visual fast/slow agents, and DeepSeek-R1, while substantial generic code-generation and confidence literature is removed. The novelty positioning changes to jointly learning routing and refinement.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, method, and conclusion are extensively rewritten, with new terminology and a reorganized narrative around adaptive reasoning, refinement, and training. The title, author list, and header change. Appendices are reorganized around APIs, prompts, rewards, and execution analysis, and dedicated Limitations and Ethics sections appear.

P2.justification: The paper changes from a single-column conference layout to two columns. Framework and case-study figures are redesigned, the confidence display changes from curves and a mean-confidence table to binned bars, and benchmark and ablation tables are substantially restructured. v1's algorithm listing disappears; v3 adds a duration chart, an API listing, and multiple formatted prompt panels.

improvement.justification: v3 strengthens empirical support through relevant agentic comparisons, explicit accuracy-runtime controls (Table 2), and training/refinement ablations (Table 4), improving on v1's output-length and routing summaries. These gains are tempered by lost hardware disclosure and illustrated failure evidence. The training conclusion also overgeneralizes: v3 Table 4 reports 58.1% for Qwen2.5-VL with SFT plus refinement versus 56.7% with SFT, GRPO, and refinement on VideoMME. The net gain is positive but limited by uneven reporting and interpretation.
